LangGraph Contents Cheatsheet

Stateful, cyclic, multi-agent orchestration

LangGraph

A hands-on guide to building stateful AI workflows with graphs—from simple chatbots through memory, control flow, and multi-agent systems to a complete production case study.

Narrated by The Crafter Eight chapters, one appendix, and a cheatsheet Grounded in LangGraph’s source and official documentation

Resume reading →

Contents

  1. 01Why LangGraph?Limitations of linear chains, when to choose LangGraph, and the core value of stateful cyclic orchestration
  2. 02Core ConceptsNodes, edges, state, reducers, channels, and the StateGraph builder
  3. 03Building Your First GraphEnvironment setup, a simple chatbot, tool calling, and graph visualization
  4. 04State and MemorySchemas, reducers, checkpointing, short-term and long-term memory, summarization
  5. 05Control Flow PatternsConditional routing, loops, retries, human-in-the-loop, breakpoints, and time-travel debugging
  6. 06Multi-Agent SystemsSubgraphs, supervisor and peer patterns, map-reduce, and a research assistant agent
  7. 07Production PatternsStreaming, LangSmith observability, deployment options, error handling, durable execution
  8. 08Case Study: A QA Agent Over Knowledge GraphsEnd-to-end pipeline with intent detection, Cypher generation, Neo4j, and Streamlit
  9. AAppendix: LangChain + LangGraph TogetherLoaders, vector stores, model interfaces, and the recommended production architecture
  10. ◊CheatsheetStateGraph API, key imports, patterns, and the decision tree on one page
How to read this

Chapters 1–3 build the mental model and get you running. Chapters 4–5 add the stateful power—memory and control flow. Chapters 6–7 scale up to multi-agent and production. Chapter 8 ties it all together in one realistic project. The appendix bridges LangChain and LangGraph for existing users. Arrow keys turn pages, ↑ returns here.
